## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Samathavāra* ("How each offense is settled") is the fifteenth section of the first major division of the *Parivāra*, the handbook of analytical summaries and pedagogical catechisms appended to the Pali *Vinayapiṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. Functioning as a technical monastic analysis, the text systematically examines the monastic offenses by correlating them with the seven methods of settling legal questions or disputes (*adhikaraṇasamatha*) [SuttaCentral]. Modern translations cataloged on SuttaCentral include an English rendering by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallel versions are listed on SuttaCentral, but automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus reveals 144 matching passages shared across 23 other Pali texts, demonstrating its extensive internal reuse of standard Vinaya formulations [DharmaNexus]. Its closest textual relationships occur within the *Parivāra* itself, most notably with the *Antarapeyyāla* (Pvr 4, sharing 44 matches and over 5,700 characters, with long shared sequences such as §2.2–3.1 matching §71.14–72.1), the *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5, 14 matches), other *Samathavāra* chapters (such as Pvr 2.15 and Pvr 2.7), and various *Samuccayavāra* and *Samuṭṭhānavāra* sections [DharmaNexus]. Text reuse also extends to late canonical or paracanonical question-and-answer texts, including the *Saṅgāyana-puccha vissajjanā Vinayapiṭaka* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus identifies segments matching the Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. The secondary literature retrieved in the research dossier does not discuss this specific chapter, touching instead on the homonymous meditation term *samatha* (calm or tranquility meditation), the *Samatha-khandhaka* of the *Cullavagga*, or the master Śamathadeva.
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
